mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate margins and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 3.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and investor pessimism, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO YoY drops by more than 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% YoY and retail sales (RSAFS) also increase by more than 5% YoY, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST YoY > 10% and RSAFS YoY > 5% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which can lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, which can lead to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a supply-side contraction with tightening monetary policy, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and investor pessimism, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: supply-side contraction with tightening monetary policy
failure_condition: If INDPRO < 0% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.
